meta.title: About ONDA Life — What It Does and Who Builds It
meta.description: ONDA Life is an iPhone app that helps you notice your nervous-system state and train it with breathing: your own trend, not a stress score. Who builds it and how.
meta.ogImageAlt: ONDA Life — an iPhone app for breathing with live heart-rhythm feedback.

title: About ONDA Life
lead: In short: ONDA Life is an iPhone app that helps you notice the state of your nervous system and train it with breathing. We don’t give scores like “stress 55%”. We show your own trend and give you a practice to work with it.
principle: Our principle: don’t track stress — train self-regulation.

items.d: ONDA builds a baseline from your heart rate and HRV (heart rate variability) history in Apple Health — from Apple Watch or another device that syncs its data there. Every day it compares you with you, not with averaged tables.
With Apple Watch you see in real time how your breathing changes your heart rhythm, and you learn to find a calm, even rhythm.
No watch? ONDA measures your pulse with the iPhone camera.
Mostly 3–12 minutes, a few up to 30: breathing, body attention, micro-movements, contemplation. If your readings stay steady, ONDA occasionally invites you to a short camera check-in or a practice.

The practices form a route: from grounding in the body to clarity and inner support. The level metaphors are figurative language for experience, not medical stages. Regular practice earns OND, the app’s game currency; it cannot be withdrawn as money.

basis.heading: What ONDA is built on
basis.p1: The evidence-based part of ONDA is slow (resonance) breathing and HRV biofeedback — among the most studied ways to influence the autonomic nervous system. The details, with sources, are in [Science](/science).
basis.p2: We are honest about the limits too: HRV from watches and rings is an estimate, not a medical measurement; one morning means nothing — your trend is what matters; low HRV is most often a reaction to short sleep, alcohol, illness or training load, not a diagnosis. See [Why is my HRV low?](/science/questions/why-is-my-hrv-low)

items.d: Every claim in the science section rests on a source with a DOI and a verbatim quote. We say who funded a study, flag single studies, and write “not shown” when there is no data.

[Scores](/reviews) follow one open [methodology](/reviews/methodology). Manufacturer-run studies don’t count as evidence. If a manufacturer claims clinical proof the product doesn’t have, we lower the score and quote their wording. Brands can’t pay for a score; any affiliate link is labelled and doesn’t affect the score.
Our tools are available in Claude and ChatGPT: device comparison, breathing practices, HRV by age. More on the [ONDA in AI apps](/ai-apps) page.

privacy.heading: Privacy
items: Your progress and diary are stored on your device.
Heart rate and HRV values are not sent to analytics.
You don’t need an account to do the practices.

person.heading: The person behind ONDA
person.p1: ONDA Life was created by Yakiv Bilenko — architect and Gestalt therapist.
person.p2: For more than 20 years he has designed physical environments: housing, public and industrial buildings, interiors, landscapes. For more than 10 years he has also worked as a Gestalt therapist and coach, building programs to restore physical, mental and emotional resources.
person.p3: ONDA continues a question that links both professions: how a person’s outer environment and inner state shape each other. The app is a tool for working with your “inner architecture” with the same care an architect brings to a building.

company.heading: Company
company.p1: ONDA Life is a product of Onda Life LLC (USA). The founder lives and works in Avilés (Asturias, Spain).
company.p2: ONDA is a tool for self-guided practice and self-observation. It is not a medical device, not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for care from a doctor or psychotherapist.
company.emergency: If you have worrying symptoms — chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, or an irregular heartbeat that doesn’t settle — seek emergency care.
